stories.title: A federated learning framework for cross-domain e-commerce behavior prediction based on adaptive aggregation and differential privacy
stories.description: Cross-domain e-commerce behavior prediction, inferring what a shopper will click, search for, or buy as they drift across several platforms, sits at the heart of personalization and conversion, yet the data that makes it valuable is locked inside competing platform silos. Three obstacles recur, and, to our reading, they are coupled rather than separate. Heterogeneity across platforms skews local updates and biases any single global model; the privacy-utility trade-off forced by data-protection law means the noise needed for a tight budget erodes the very signals personalization rests on; and non-IID data drags federated convergence out, occasionally to the point of divergence. We propose AAPD-FedRec (Adaptive Aggregation and Privacy-Differential Federated Recommender), whose name marks its two pillars, and which tackles the three obstacles together because, in practice, fixing one in isolation tends to reopen another. Three modules share the work: an adaptive aggregator answers heterogeneity by weighting client updates through a composite signal of data quality, gradient direction consistency, and historical update stability, displacing the volume-only rule of FedAvg; a sensitivity-aware scheduler answers the privacy-utility tension by spreading a fixed total budget non-uniformly across rounds and clients, paired with gradient clipping and Gaussian perturbation, while the moments accountant tracks cumulative privacy loss with closed-form $$(\varepsilon ,\delta )$$ guarantees. A third module, a domain-aware embedding alignment layer, reconciles heterogeneous feature spaces across platforms without exchanging raw representations, so the three components attack the three obstacles in concert rather than one at a time. Experiments on Amazon and Taobao cross-domain partitions show that AAPD-FedRec converges in roughly half the rounds required by competing baselines, recovers AUC at $$0.7714$$ under $$\varepsilon =1$$ where DP-FedAvg drops to $$0.6921$$, and limits membership-inference attacker advantage to $$0.041$$ at the same budget. Ablations confirm that the three contribution dimensions act complementarily rather than redundantly. The framework offers a practical path toward joint behavior modeling for cross-border platforms operating under strict regulatory constraints, with potential transfer to financial risk control, medical recommendation, and educational analytics.

stories.title: Nucleosomes and IDRs suppress promiscuous GCN4 binding on minichromosomes
stories.description: Eukaryotic sequence-specific transcription factors (TFs) must find their cognate DNA targets hidden in genomic chromatin amid an excess of nonspecific sequences and degenerate motifs. Although static TF interactions with nucleosomal targets have been elucidated, how TFs efficiently search for cognate sites within native gene-sized chromatin domains has been unclear. Here we used purified Saccharomyces cerevisiae HIS3 minichromosomes and single-molecule imaging to compare association and dissociation kinetics of transcription activator GCN4 on chromatin and naked genomic DNA. GCN4 displays widespread and stable off-target binding on bare DNA because of entrapment by degenerate sites and interactions with nonspecific DNA of increasing length, indicative of one-dimensional (1D) diffusion. Nucleosome organization on the minichromosome reduces promiscuous GCN4 residence times by obstructing TF association and restricting 1D target search within nucleosome-free regions. Furthermore, the intrinsically disordered GCN4 activation domain independently enhances targeting efficiency and specificity by accelerating association–dissociation kinetics in vitro and in living cells. Altogether, both nucleosome organization and activation domains independently suppress promiscuous GCN4 binding, which, if unchecked, may cause aberrant cryptic transcription known to occur upon chromatin disruptions. Wei et al. measure single-molecule kinetics of transcription factor GCN4 on purified yeast minichromosomes to reveal that both nucleosomes and transcription factor intrinsically disordered regions facilitate GCN4 target search on native chromatin by shortening its promiscuous binding.

stories.title: Psychological capital links social support to student outcomes in both economically disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged college students
stories.description: Drawing on social support theory, positive psychology, and resource-based perspectives, this study examined whether psychological capital (PsyCap) mediates the relationships among teacher support, peer support, and family cohesion and two student outcomes—meaning in life and learning engagement—as well as whether these mediating pathways differ between economically disadvantaged and economically non-disadvantaged college students. Data were collected through an online survey from 1756 students, of whom 646 were disadvantaged and 1110 non-disadvantaged, studying at a university in southern China. Structural equation modeling and multi-group analysis showed that PsyCap mediated several pathways linking social support and family cohesion to student outcomes, although the significance and magnitude of these indirect effects varied across economic groups. These findings highlight the role of PsyCap as a protective psychological resource, particularly for economically disadvantaged students, and provide practical implications for designing targeted interventions to strengthen student well-being and learning engagement.

stories.title: Neural regulation of tumor immunity: emerging opportunities to enhance cancer immunotherapy
stories.description: The nervous system is a key regulator of cancer immunity, influencing tumor development and treatment response through neuroimmune interactions. Both peripheral and central circuits transmit neural signals that directly influence immune cell recruitment, activation, and effector function within the tumor microenvironment. Evidences indicate that sympathetic, parasympathetic, sensory neurons, and glial cells actively reshape the immune landscape through neurotransmitters and neuromodulators. Central neural circuits, such as catecholaminergic and stress-responsive pathways, further integrate psychological states and autonomic outflow to systemically reprogram immunity. However, how these diverse neural signals converge with tumor and immune cell interactions remains poorly defined. This Review synthesizes current advances across four dimensions: the roles of peripheral neurons and central neural circuits in cancer immunity; glial cell contributions to immunosuppression and tumor progression; reciprocal influences of tumor cells on neural remodeling; and neuron-independent neural signaling through immune-expressed adrenergic, cholinergic, and peptidergic receptors. We highlight that perineural invasion, tumor innervation heterogeneity, and receptor subtype-specific signaling are key factors in immune evasion and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitor. By integrating these perspectives, this Review establishes the nervous system as a critical yet underexplored dimension of cancer immunology and proposes that context-defined and receptor-specific modulation of selected neuroimmune pathways may enhance immunotherapy. Cancer remains a substantial global health challenge, with traditional treatments often limited by recurrence and resistance. Recent advances in immunotherapy have shifted focus toward restoring host antitumor immunity; however, clinical efficacy varies due to immune evasion and suppressive tumor microenvironments. This Review explores the emerging role of neural regulation in cancer, highlighting how tumor innervation and neurotransmitter signaling influence immune cell dynamics and therapeutic responses. Researchers detail how adrenergic, cholinergic, and peptidergic signaling pathways, along with glial cell contributions, create a neuroimmune landscape that supports cancer progression. Key findings reveal that tumor-derived exosomes and neural remodeling promote immune evasion, whereas central neural circuits modulate systemic immunity. These insights underscore the potential of targeting neuroimmune pathways to enhance immunotherapy efficacy. This summary was initially drafted using artificial intelligence, then revised and fact-checked by the author.

stories.title: Fossil shark scales reveal how ocean productivity shapes shark populations
stories.description:
Long before intensive human fishing began, Pacific reefs naturally supported far more sharks than Caribbean reefs, according to a new study. The findings, based on an analysis of fossilized shark scales, suggest that differences in ocean productivity – and not fishing alone – have shaped shark populations for thousands of years, information that could guide future conservation efforts. Shark populations have declined worldwide, especially on coral reefs, where many species are now at high risk of extinction. However, conservation efforts have been hindered by a lack of historical baselines showing what healthy shark populations looked like before widespread human impacts, making it difficult to set realistic conservation and recovery goals. To address this gap, Erin Dillon and colleagues reconstructed reef shark communities spanning the past 7,000 years by analyzing fossilized shark dermal denticles – tiny tooth-like scales preserved in coral reef sediments. Denticle abundance in reef sediments closely reflects shark populations.
 
Dillon et al. collected fossil denticles from the Caribbean and Pacific coasts of Panama, two neighboring regions with contrasting ocean conditions and levels of human activity but many of the same shark species. By comparing ancient (~7 to 3 ka) and recent (past ~100 years) sediments, the authors were able to determine natural baselines for reef shark populations and evaluate how environmental conditions and human pressures have shaped their decline over time. The findings revealed that healthy reef shark populations naturally differed between Pacific and Caribbean reefs. Pacific reefs supported about 20 times more sharks than Caribbean reefs thousands of years before intensive fishing. Since then, Caribbean shark populations, particularly fast-swimming pelagic species, have declined by roughly 75%, while Pacific populations have remained comparatively stable, despite experiencing higher historical fishing pressure.  As a result, the gap between the two regions has widened dramatically, with modern Pacific reefs now supporting about 100 times more sharks than comparable Caribbean reefs. Dillon et al. conclude that differences in ocean productivity have long played a crucial role in determining how many sharks a reef can naturally support. The Pacific coast of Panama, fueled by nutrient-rich seasonal upwelling, has historically sustained much larger shark populations and appears more resilient to human impacts than the less productive Caribbean, where shark populations have declined far more dramatically. These findings suggest that conservation goals should be tailored to regional ecological conditions rather than applying a single baseline across different ecosystems. In a related Perspective, Peter Roopnarine discusses the study in greater detail.

stories.title: iFixit's Galaxy Z Fold8 Teardown is a Preview of Apple's Foldable Challenges
stories.description: Samsung launched new foldable smartphones earlier this month, including the Galaxy Z Fold8. If you didn't know it was a Samsung device, you might look at it and think it's Apple's foldable because it matches rumors about the iPhone Ultra so well. The Z Fold8 is likely to be the closest competitor to the foldable iPhone Ultra, which makes iFixit's teardown of Samsung's smartphone an interesting read.

stories.title: Apple Says iPhone X is Now Obsolete
stories.description: Apple today added the iPhone X and the 2018 model of the 15-inch MacBook Pro to its obsolete products list, according to an updated support document. Released in November 2017, the iPhone X was the first iPhone with an OLED display and Face ID. The lack of a Touch ID home button resulted in the device having a more edge-to-edge screen with a notch for the front camera and Face ID sensors. The device featured a premium design with a glass back and a stainless steel frame.
